newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin says to continue NATO talks, visit Germany.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin says to continue NATO talks, visit Germany.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin said on Saturday he agreed at talks with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl to continue seeking ways to settle Russia's differences with the West over the eastward expansion of NATO.
Interfax news agency said Yeltsin told his spokesman, Sergei Yastrzhembsky, he had agreed to visit Germany in April.
Yastrzhembsky told Interfax both leaders were satisfied with the meeting, which covered bilateral relations and European security, especially the enlargement of NATO.

"We sought a settlement of this issue. We agreed to continue discussion in the future on the theme 'Russia and NATO'," Yastrzhembsky quoted the Russian President as saying, according to Interfax and Itar-Tass news agencies.
The two leaders also agreed to cooperate closely in the preparation of the next meeting of the Group of Seven (G7) rich nations and Russia.

Kohl is the first Western leader to meet the 65-year-old Yeltsin since he underwent a heart bypass operation on November 5. Yeltsin, meeting Kohl at the helipad at the Rus hunting lodge outside Moscow, looked tired in television footage but pleased to see the chancellor, whom he regards as a personal friend.
